messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm), pure water’s freezing (melting) point is **about –2 °C**.  
This is slightly below the standard 0 °C freezing point at 1 atm because the ice–water equilibrium line on the phase diagram slopes downward with decreasing pressure.  At 10 kPa the equilibrium temperature is roughly 271 K (≈ –2 °C).
